# prompt - inserting the prompt
```{r}
# prompt <- R"(Role: You are an expert systematic review screener specializing in vaccinology and epidemiology. Task: Evaluate whether the study meets the eligibility criteria below, based strictly on its title and abstract.
# Eligibility Criteria. Inclusion Criteria (Must meet ALL of the following):
# Population: Human participants of any age, health status, or vaccination history.
# Intervention: Explicitly evaluates the effects, efficacy, or safety of a COVID-19 vaccine. The study MUST report specific outcome data for COVID-19 vaccines. Include only studies that evaluate any of the following vaccines, inkludert oppfriskningsdoser (boostere):
# o mRNA-vaksiner: Moderna (Spikevax), neste generasjon mRNA (mNEXSPIKE), Pfizer/BioNTech (Comirnaty).
# o Proteinbaserte subenhetsvaksiner: HIPRA / Bimervax, Novavax (Nuvaxovid, Novavax, Covovax), Sanofi (VidPrevtyn).
# o sa-mRNA-vaksiner: Arcturus (Kostaive), inkludert zapomeran.
# If a study evaluates multiple COVID-19 vaccines, but evaluates at least one of the vaccines mentioned above, include the study.
# Comparator: Any comparator or no comparator is acceptable.
# Eligible Study Designs: Experimental: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs), non-randomized studies, quasi-experimental studies.
# Observational: Prospective/retrospective cohort studies, population-based studies, registry-based studies, case-control, and nested case-control studies.
# Secondary research/Other: Systematic reviews, meta-analyses, post-marketing safety evaluations, and clinical guidelines explicitly based on systematic reviews.
# Exclusion Criteria (Exclude if ANY of the following apply):
# Missing Information: Exclude if any of the following apply: 1) the title and abstract lack sufficient detail to confirm eligibility; 2) if the abstract is missing, unless the title explicitly specifies an eligible study design evaluating COVID-19 vaccines; 3) There is no information provided in the title; 4) the title or abstract does not clearly indicate that the study evaluates COVID-19 vaccines.
# Out of Scope: Non-human studies; studies not evaluating/reporting specific effects, efficacy, or safety data for COVID-19 vaccines.
# Ineligible Study Designs: Cross-sectional studies; surveys or self-reported data lacking outcome validation; qualitative studies; narrative (non-systematic) reviews; scoping reviews; mapping reviews; case reports; case series; editorials; conference proceedings; commentaries; replies to editor; and letters without original data.
# Constraints & Rules: Base your decision ONLY on the provided title and abstract. Full-text evaluation is not possible to confirm eligibility.
# Include a study ONLY if every inclusion criterion is met and no exclusion criterion applies.
# Required Output Format
# Decision: [Include / Exclude]
# Primary Reason: [Briefly state the core reason for the decision]
# Rationale: [Provide a concise, step-by-step breakdown referencing specific criteria])"
```

# Loading the references
```{r}
COVID1_ES_references <- read_ris_to_dataframe("data//LEVAK_COVID_ES_1_202608.txt")
COVID1_ES_references <- readRDS("data/COVID1_ES_references.RData")


view(COVID1_ES_references)
colnames(COVID1_ES_references)

# saving the references in RData and Excel formats
saveRDS(COVID1_ES_references, file = "data/COVID1_ES_references.RData")
write.xlsx(COVID1_ES_references, "data/COVID1_ES_references.xlsx")
```

```{r}
# splitting the references into chunks of 200
chunks <- split(COVID1_ES_references, ceiling(seq_along(1:nrow(COVID1_ES_references))/200))

# creating the folder for the outputs
dir.create("screening_chunks", showWarnings = FALSE)

# looping through each chunk and saving it as a separate RData file
for (i in seq_along(chunks)) {
    f <- file.path("screening_chunks", sprintf("chunk_%03d.rds", i))
    if (file.exists(f)) next 

    res <- tryCatch(
        tabscreen_gpt(
         data = chunks[[i]],
         prompt = prompt,
         studyid = record_id,
         abstract = abstract,
         model = "gpt-5-mini",
         reps = 1,
         decision_description = TRUE
    ),
    error = function(e) { message("Bolk ", i, " feilet: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL }
)
    if (!is.null(res)) saveRDS(res, f)
}
```

 #  putting all the chunks together-saving the chunk files 
```{r}
chunk_files <- list.files("screening_chunks", full.names = TRUE)

view(chunk_files)
saveRDS(chunk_files, "outputs/chunk_files.RData")
write_xlsx(data.frame(chunk_files), "outputs/chunk_files.xlsx")
readxlsx("outputs/chunk_files.xlsx")
```

# creating the compiled screening results by combining all the chunk files
```{r}
COVID1_ES_screening_results <- purrr::map(chunk_files, \(f) readRDS(f)$answer_data) |>
  purrr::list_rbind()
```

# inspecting the completeness of the screening results

```{r}
#successful and failed rows
successful_references <- purrr::map(chunk_files, \(f) readRDS(f)$answer_data) |> purrr::list_rbind()
errors <- purrr::map(chunk_files, \(f) readRDS(f)$error_data) |> purrr::list_rbind()

#sanity checks
length(chunks) == length(chunk_files) # TRUE, the number of chunks is equal to the number of chunk files
nrow(COVID1_ES_references) # checking the number of references = 12030
nrow(successful_references); n_distinct(successful_references$studyid) # no duplicates 
sum(is.na(successful_references$decision_binary)) # checking for missing decisions = 209
nrow(errors) # checking the number of errors = 209
names(errors) # inspect the error columns/messages
```

# extracting the successful and failed references
```{r}
# IDs with a valid decision (successful references)
ok_ids <- successful_references |>
  filter(!is.na(decision_binary)) |>
  pull(studyid) |>
  unique() |>
  as.character()

# references NOT screened (covers failed calls AND missing chunks)
not_screened <- COVID1_ES_references |>
  filter(!as.character(record_id) %in% ok_ids)
  nrow(not_screened) # 209 references not screened successfully
  view(not_screened)

# valid results from the first run, to keep
screened_1 <- successful_references |> filter(!is.na(decision_binary))
```

# re-run the loop for the failed references 
Use a separate folder so the first-run files stay untouched:

```{r}
dir.create("screening_chunks_retry", showWarnings = FALSE)
chunks_retry <- split(not_screened, ceiling(seq_along(nrow(not_screened))/200)) # putting the chunks of the failed references into chunks of 200

# the loop for the failed references
for (i in seq_along(chunks_retry)) {
  f <- file.path("screening_chunks_retry", sprintf("chunk_%03d.rds", i))
  if (file.exists(f)) next

  res <- tryCatch(
    tabscreen_gpt(
      data = chunks_retry[[i]],
      prompt = prompt,
      studyid = record_id,
      abstract = abstract,
      model = "gpt-5-mini",
      reps = 1,
      decision_description = TRUE
    ),
    error = function(e) { message("Chunk ", i, " failed: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL }
  )
  if (!is.null(res)) saveRDS(res, f)
}
```

It is important to keep the same prompt and model for the re-run to ensure consistency in the screening process.

# merge and verify
```{r}
retry_files <- list.files("screening_chunks_retry", full.names = TRUE, pattern = "\\.rds$")

screened_retry <- purrr::map(retry_files, \(f) readRDS(f)$answer_data) |>
  purrr::list_rbind() |>
  filter(!is.na(decision_binary))
saveRDS(screened_retry, "outputs/screened_retry.RData")
openxlsx::write.xlsx(screened_retry, "outputs/screened_retry.xlsx")

COVID1_ES_screening_results <- bind_rows(screened_1, screened_retry) #combining the results from the first run and the re-run

# should be TRUE, and 0
nrow(COVID1_ES_screening_results) == nrow(COVID1_ES_references)
setdiff(as.character(COVID1_ES_references$record_id),
        as.character(COVID1_ES_screening_results$studyid))

saveRDS(COVID1_ES_screening_results, "outputs/COVID1_ES_screening_results.RData")
openxlsx::write.xlsx(COVID1_ES_screening_results, "outputs/COVID1_ES_screening_results.xlsx")

nrow(COVID1_ES_screening_results) # 12030
sum(is.na(COVID1_ES_screening_results$decision_binary)) # 0 meaning all references have been screened successfully
```
